subject: Capacity tradeoffs & prioritization matrix for Polaris Health dedicated pool
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: dedicated GPU sizing & prioritization for Polaris deal (DL-2026-0987)

Team —

Polaris Health is pushing for a dedicated pool commitment as part of their PPO rollout. Deal asks: 8 sustained A100-80GB equivalent vGPUs with a 2-node burst buffer for peak ETL windows, plus strict data residency in us-west. They want guaranteed throughput during business hours and a fallback policy if we run into contention.

Can you confirm whether we can:
- Reserve 8 units in us-west permanently under Dedicated?
- Offer a burst slice (2 nodes) that can preempt lower-priority workloads?
- Add an SLA clause for guaranteed p99 latency during their business hours (8am–8pm PT)?

Attached: capacity_request_sheet.xlsx (initial estimates).

I need clear options we can present to Polaris by end of day Wednesday so contracts can close.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated GPU sizing & prioritization for Polaris deal (DL-2026-0987)

Olga —

Thanks for the details. Quick operational assessment:

1) Capacity: We have two options that are realistic today in us-west:
   a) Strict reservation: carve 8 A100-equivalent instances from the Dedicated pool. This is the cleanest for SLAs but reduces available capacity for sound-alike deals (will impact 3 other pending commitments).
   b) Reservation + burst policy: reserve 6 guaranteed units + a 2-node burst that is preemptible. This mitigates impact to other committed customers.

2) SLA feasibility: We can commit to a p99 latency SLA during business hours only if the pool is fully reserved or if the on-call team is allowed to prioritize their routing (hard priority). Adding a latency SLA requires a monthly availability credit clause and a higher price.

3) Risk: If we accept strict reservation for Polaris without an offset (commit/price uplift or capacity trading), we will likely need to delay onboarding for a smaller strategic customer (Nimbus AI, deal in flight) or reduce their burst allowance. Expect an internal escalation from Product/CS if we take that route.

Recommendation: Offer option (b) with clear tiers: guaranteed (6), burst (2 preemptible), plus an overnight warm-up for model KV caches. Provide a priced uplift for strict reservation if they require it.

I'll draft the allocation matrix and impact table. Need confirmation on whether Sales wants to prioritize closing Polaris over Nimbus.

—Vivek
Director, Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: polaris_map_prioritization.pdf (planning sketch)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: James Tan <james.tan@polarishealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed capacity approach and options for Polaris (DL-2026-0987)

James / Contracts —

Thanks for the productive discovery call last week. Quick note to share what our ops team recommended and to lay out 2 options so you can choose what fits your risk profile.

Option A — Guaranteed pool (higher price):
- 8 A100-equivalent Dedicated units reserved in us-west
- SLA: p99 latency guarantee during business hours (8am–8pm PT)
- Price uplift: +35% on top of standard dedicated rate
- No preemption; zero impact to performance during business hours

Option B — Hybrid (recommended):
- 6 guaranteed Dedicated units + 2 preemptible burst nodes
- SLA: best-effort during burst windows; guaranteed for the 6 units
- Price uplift: +18% on standard dedicated rate

If you need strict reservation for regulatory reasons (we saw HIPAA mentioned), we can pursue Option A but will need the signed commitment and an immediate capacity booking. Attached is our internal prioritization sketch so you can see tradeoffs.

Next steps: pick Option A or B by Wednesday, Nov 19 so we can lock the fleet allocation. I copied our capacity lead (Vivek) in case you have technical questions.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_request_sheet.xlsx

From: James Tan <james.tan@polarishealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@polarishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed capacity approach and options for Polaris (DL-2026-0987)

Olga —

Thanks for the options. A few clarifications:
- Polaris requires strict performance for clinical inference windows (7am–7pm PT). HIPAA compliance also pushes us toward minimizing preemption risk.
- We can accept Option A if you can include a short-term credit if you fail to meet p99 SLA in the first 90 days (pilot grace period).
- We need evidence of data residency + audit logs for any Dedicated deployment (SOC2 + audit export).

Contracts is looped for redlines. Can you confirm lead time for a strict reservation if we sign tomorrow?

Thanks,
James Tan
Head of SRE | Polaris Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed capacity approach and options for Polaris (DL-2026-0987)

All —

If Polaris needs Option A for compliance, Sales is willing to accommodate but we need to protect our supply. Proposed commercial guardrails:
- 12-month minimum term for strict reservation; 6-month for hybrid (Option B)
- 30% non-refundable deposit to be allocated immediately upon contract signature (this funds hold on hardware)
- If Polaris signs Option A, offer a 90-day pilot SLA credit (capped) as requested, and pass-through SOC2 evidence.

Operational ask to Capacity: Vivek — if Polaris signs Option A, what exactly moves off the table? Which pending deals (IDs) will be rescheduled or reduced? I need a short impact summary to include in the executive approval packet.

—Marissa
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, James Tan <james.tan@polarishealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@polarishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Final: allocation decision & next steps (DL-2026-0987)

Team / James —

Summary and decision: Polaris has elected Option A (strict reservation) with the 12-month term and the 30% deposit. We will accept the 90-day pilot SLA credit (cap to be included in the contract redline).

Operational impact: Vivek provided the allocation plan inline — we will carve 8 units from the us-west spare pool and temporarily reduce the burst allocation for Deal DL-2026-1021 (Nimbus AI). Nimbus will maintain 4 guaranteed units but their burst will be reduced from 4 to 2 until Q1 ramp. This avoids delaying Nimbus onboarding but reduces their peak headroom.

Action items:
- Vivek: run the SLA playbook and schedule a dry-run for latency testing next week; share the impact table for exec packet (by EOD Monday).
- Contracts: push the redline with SLA credit clause and SOC2 evidence request; attach signed deposit invoice flow.
- Olga: send Polaris the deposit invoice link and confirm start date once deposit clears.

James — welcome aboard. We will attach the signed_sla_term_redline.pdf and the capacity_request_sheet.xlsx to the contract. Expect emails from Contracts with DocuSign links within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Product & Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

Attachments: signed_sla_term_redline.pdf
